articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms for Producing Equations in Physics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Based at the prospective scenario that computers might to replace humans, emerge the idea that them can carry out jobs as a scientist does. Thus, one might to expect that for example machine learning can be a serious competitor of humans as to produce research even of cutting edge quality. In this paper, some algorithms based at artificial neural networks are employed to produce known physics based at coincidences with artificial models generated by Machine Learning approach.

articleTitle: Generation and Accuracy Evaluation of Disaster Situation Maps Using Damage-Scale Index: DI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In the event of an earthquake, it is necessary to quickly assess the damage caused by house collapses. Although this Damage-Scale index has been developed by Shiraishi et al. Therefore, this study evaluates the accuracy of automatically generated maps using the Damage-Scale Index (DI) by comparing them with the disaster damage map of the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake that occurred on January 1, 2024 on the Noto Peninsula in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan. The accuracy of the map generated automatically using the Damage-Scale Index DI was evaluated by comparing it with a field surveyed disaster damage map for the Noto Peninsula earthquake that occurred on January 1, 2024. The accuracy of the map generated by this index was sufficient to detect damaged houses, and 14 of the 15 houses with collapsed damage (D5) were legitimately identified as damaged. Of the 16 houses with no collapsed damage (D0-D4), 14 were justifiably assessed as undamaged. Damage Grade D5 (equivalent to a Damage Index of 0.8 or higher) was classified as “house collapse damage” and the rest (D0-D4) as “no house collapse damage” in EMS-98, which is defined as an index of damage scale. The DI for houses with D5 was 0.138, a large value. Therefore, it was concluded that the respondents correctly recognized the damage. This analysis method is a highly effective index in the initial response, where a quick response is required.

articleTitle: YOLO-Based Oil Palm FFB Ripeness Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The palm oil industry is a huge contributor to Malaysia's economic growth. Adopting new technologies such as AI to optimize the different processes involved in the palm oil industry and minimizing the problems such as high time consumption and labor intensiveness associated with the traditional ways of handling fruits in the industry will further assist the economic growth of Malaysia and will help reduce negative environmental effects. This research offers insights on the related literature and employs a YOLOv10-S model with mAP (mean average precision) of 0.95 for detecting ripe FFB (fresh fruit bunch) from unripe FFB. After the completion of the training the model was exported and used in an interface.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Cost Virtual Rifle Shooting Simulator for the Peruvian Army Military School
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Training personnel in the use of weapons is crucial for military effectiveness, but traditional methods require significant investments in firearms and ammunition. This challenge is particularly evident in developing countries, where military budgets are constrained. To address this, virtual rifle shooting simulators offer a cost-effective solution for enhancing military training. This paper presents the design and implementation of a low-cost virtual rifle shooting simulator for the Peruvian Army Military School. The system integrates a light automatic rifle equipped with a laser system and a computer vision-based detection mechanism for accurate shot analysis in various training environments. Additionally, an electrical recoil simulation system enhances the realism of the training experience. The proposed system was validated through shot detection and laser signal recognition tests, demonstrating high accuracy in different lighting conditions. The entire prototype was developed at a cost of USD 1,100, significantly reducing the expenses associated with traditional training methods while maintaining performance standards. This research contributes to the development of affordable and portable military training simulators, enabling broader access to advanced training technologies.

articleTitle: A Study to Integrate EV Charging Station in an Industrial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: To minimize the environmental impact and as well as the dependency on oil imports EVs playa vital role. However, the growing number of electric vehicles poses a maj or risk to the electricity distribution network. The growing need for electricity required by EV s might interfere with the uninterrupted operation of the power supply system. To ensure the reliable and safe operation of the power distribution network, the effects of EV charging stations on the power grid need to be investigated. Recently, significant research has been done regarding the effects of EV charging stations on the power grid. This article proposes a methodology to design an EV charging station in an industrial network considering the operational challenges including bus voltage violations, motor starting issues, and distribution line overloading. A tentative Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) based solution has also been proposed to overcome such adverse impacts in designing the charging station with the increased number of EVs.

articleTitle: Predictive Model of Next Global Pandemic Based in Perceptron and Shannon Entropy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Based at the idea that global pandemic and its central peak of infections had as main cause the conjunction of variables derived from a kind of disorder, then one might to expect that data would be described by the Shannon entropy. This paper has assumed a simple trapezoid whose vertexes would denote the peaks of Omicron and possible next pandemic. From this, the Shannon entropy of possible next global pandemic is directly related to the possible peak of infections as function of Omicron peak. With this, perceptron is constructed in order to predict the possible peak of infections of next pandemic. A kind of asymmetry between Covid-19 and next possible global pandemic was found.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Traditional CSS and UAV -based Virtual CSS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Cooperative spectrum sensing (CSS) in cognitive radio networks offers an effective approach to enhance throughput, spectral efficiency, and energy efficiency. However, increasing the number of secondary users also raises energy consumption, leading to a decrease in energy efficiency. To address this, we propose a novel technique using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for cooperative spectrum sensing to reduce energy consumption while improving throughput and energy efficiency in cognitive radio networks. In this paper, we compare the throughput performance of traditional CSS with UAV-based virtual CSS. Simulation results demonstrate that UAV-based CSS outperforms traditional CSS in terms of throughput. The study also identifies the optimal fusion rule, the ideal number of UAV slots and secondary users, and the optimal detection threshold for improving wireless network performance.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of New Visible Index on Remote Sensing for Estimating House Damage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: When earthquake damage occurs, it is extremely important to quickly identify the presence or absence of such damage. In this study, we developed and evaluated a new remote sensing index to automatically determine “damage” by image analysis when damage greater than partial destruction of a house by an earthquake or tsunami occurs. The accuracy of the houses estimated as “damaged” by this index was high and sufficient for the initial assessment of damage. The results of this research are expected to be utilized for more rapid damage assessment after a disaster.

articleTitle: Design of X Band Double Balance Mixer for Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this study, a mixer circuit designed to operate within the X-band frequency range of 8–9 GHz has been developed. The design aims to provide a cost-effective and high-performance solution, incorporating a double balanced mixer using Schottky barrier diodes. The mixer design is supported by a Marchand Balun, configured in a star topology, which effectively combines the Radio Frequency and Local Oscillator signals. The mixer with the FR4 substrate material showed a conversion loss from 8.8 to 9.2 dB.

articleTitle: Battery Charger Based on Interleaved Three-Branch Converter with Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper analyzes interleaved converters in high-power systems, focusing on applications such as battery charging. Model Predictive Control (MPC) was implemented to predict system behavior and optimize control actions. The converter initially operates in constant current control (CCC) before transitioning to constant voltage control (CV C). Throughout the charging process, MPC ensures the stability of current and voltage, adjusting control variables in response to input voltage variations. The study highlights the benefits of interleaved con-verters, including reduced power losses, minimized component stress, and improved overall efficiency, making them ideal for high-demand applications such as electric vehicle charging,

articleTitle: Phenomenological Recession: From Gaussian to Bayesian Probability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: If recession is a random event, then it might be governed by probabilistic laws instead determinism, because unexpected confluence of variables showing notable changes in their behavior in time. This paper, proposes the idea that recession might be perceived as a kind of transition from a Gaussian profile to one dictated by Bayesian probabilities. Under this approach, recession exhibits its phenomenological character as observed at the chain of events and the sharpness of variables previous to its main manifestation. This would be seen as a temporal evolving whose interrelation of involved variables might be conditional among each other, triggering a fast increasing in the probability of having contraction of economical activity. The Mitchell criteria inside the framework of Machine Learning to test theoretical proposal were used. Simulations are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A Study on the three-dimensional Augmented GAN Algorithm through Object Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Computer vision has been rapidly growing alongside the advancements in artificial intelligence, with particular attention on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Among these, CartoonGAN is a model that transforms real photos into cartoon-style images. This model has a limitation in that the simplification of colors during the process of converting real photos into a cartoon style reduces the sense of depth. To address this issue, this study proposes an algorithm that enhances depth perception by clearly separating elements within the image to expand the sense of distance. Additionally, the algorithm strengthens depth perception by applying shading adjustments and a vignette mask. This approach allows for the creation of vivid and three-dimensional cartoon images by applying 3D information to otherwise flat images. Furthermore, it preserves the edges of objects to maximize the visual experience. Future research will aim to increase the applicability of the proposed algorithm to images with various conditions.

articleTitle: Implementation of Solar Based Irrigation Robotic System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In our digital world, everything around us needs to be processed to reduce human effort and make modern life easier, more practical, more convenient, and more sustainable. Nevertheless, today there are major problems as energy and water scarcity. Our scop is to design a robot uses solar energy panel fixed above our it for maintaining continuous charging to generate clean electrical power and store it in a lithium battery, this stored electricity used later for running robotic systems for efficient irrigation in big scale farms to conserve water consumption and precise crop monitoring, using many inputs data (sensor) as soil moisture sensor which consist of with two copper tubes inputs to control whether the soil is wet or dry. more sensors are used as temperature sensor and color senser. Where all sensors connected to the microcontroller (Arduino processor) which used to activate or shut down the irrigation pump and light ON /OFF Red LED or Green LED after detecting the level of crop maturity, when the microcontroller receives the signal from the color sensors, plus the temperature of weather considered in all data processing. thus, the robot can then detect crop needs more water or ready for growth up to harvesting time.

articleTitle: Improving Convolutional Neural Networks Diagnostic Ability for Malignant Skin Diseases on Diverse Skin Tones with Smooth Grad-CAM++ and Grad-CAM++
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are widely used in skin disease detection, but often perform poorly on datasets with diverse skin tones, due to the lack of skin diseases images of darker skinned people. This paper focuses on enhancing the quality of the image dataset used to train CNN models through specific types of Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mappings (Grad-CAMs) and compares the effects different types of Grad-CAM may have on skin disease diagnostic rates. Two CNN architectures (ResNet-34 and VGG-11) are compared alongside with two types of Grad-CAMs: Smooth Grad-CAM++ and Grad-CAM++. The ResNet-34 model paired with Smooth Grad-CAM++ shows the greatest improvement, with average detection accuracies between the 900th to 1000th epoch reaching 58.46% and 63.20% with standard deviations of 3.89% and 3.03%, respectively trained by the raw and refined datasets. The observed increase in accuracy highlights the efficacy of the proposed procedure in enhancing model performance for detecting skin diseases across diverse skin tones given limited dataset, offering a new potential fast and low-cost alternative lifesaving tool for early skin diseases detection.

articleTitle: Classification of Crime-related News Titles using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: News classification in the crime-related domain offers a multitude of benefits that extend beyond efficient information retrieval and crime analysis. Classified news articles can be used to educate the public about crime prevention tips, safety measures, and the importance of community involvement in crime reporting. Classifying crime news provides a rich dataset for researchers to study crime trends, patterns, and contributing factors. This evidence-based research can inform the development of effective crime prevention and intervention strategies. This paper proposes classification of crime-related news titles using machine learning models. The data was acquired from live news feeds. Methods such as TF-IDF was applied on the data to generate feature vectors. Machine learning (ML) models were trained and evaluated. ML models such as Decision Tree and Random Forest models exhibit the highest accuracy and F1 scores, suggesting that they are the most effective in predicting crime-related news titles. Both models achieved an accuracy of 99% and Fl scores of 98% and 97%, respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband RF Front - End Circuit Design for Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and performance evaluation of a four-stage X-band Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) tailored for satellite communication applications. The proposed LNA operates within the frequency range of 7.75 GHz to 8.5 GHz, covering a bandwidth of 750 MHz, which is crucial for modern satellite communication systems. The design employs discrete packaged transistors and distributed components, combined with precise input and output matching networks, to achieve an impressive noise figure of less than 0.7 dB. A maximum gain of 50 dB is obtained, with the amplifier remaining unconditionally stable from DC to 20 GHz. An electromagnetic field solver was utilized during the design process, offering a high level of accuracy over traditional closed-form approximations of microstrip lines. This ensured that the prototype met the stringent system requirements, particularly after the integration of the DC control circuitry into the PCB layout. The LNA's gain flatness across the operating frequency range is maintained at +/- 0.5 dB, demonstrating excellent performance. The measured results, including a minimum noise figure of 0.623 dB, show that the LNA is competitive with commercial alternatives. This work highlights the effectiveness of the proposed design for satellite communication systems, achieving optimal performance in terms of noise, gain, and impedance matching, while addressing the challenges associated with operating at X-band frequencies.

articleTitle: Rating, Similarity — User-Item Based Collaborative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Hybrid recommender systems involve the combi-nation of multiple recommendation strategies to improve the accuracy and robustness of recommendations outcomes. Such hybrid designs combine various methods such as collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and knowledge-based techniques to address inherent limitations in individual approaches like sparse data, scalability problems and cold start issues. By doing this, these systems employ different algorithms for personalized and context-aware recommendations that are more effective than traditional ones, thus enhancing user satisfaction and engage-ment. This paper investigates the architecture design and imple-mentation of hybrid recommender systems; it also looks at their methodologies while balancing computational efficiency against recommendation accuracy. Also, we present case studies where hybrid systems have been successfully implemented in domains such as e-commerce, entertainment or social networking, showing how flexible they can be in various application scenarios. It is found that hybrid recommender based on dynamically adapting to users' preferences and behavior changes is a promising way to achieve superior recommendation performance.

articleTitle: Robust Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Control for Frequency Regulation in Islanded Microgrids incorporating RESs and HESS using a Disturbance Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The increasing demand for integrating more renewable energy sources (RESs) into microgrids, especially isolated ones, presents significant challenges due to higher variability and uncertainties associated with these RESs, along with load variations. For instance, photovoltaic (PV) and wind energy can be significantly impacted by weather conditions, which may compromise system stability by altering its frequency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an integral terminal sliding mode control (ITSMC) combined with a disturbance observer for improved power balance and frequency regulation in islanded microgrids, taking into account the participation of hybrid energy storage systems (HESS). Additionally, using the ITSMC enhances the performance of the secondary controller in microgrid operations, further enhancing the system's flexibility and stability under sudden load variations and changing weather conditions. A genetic algorithm has been employed to optimally tune the gains of the proposed control approach and the performance of the proposed controller has been analyzed using MATLAB/Simulink. A comparative analysis between the proposed control approach and literature-suggested techniques has also been presented.

Author Keywords: robust integral terminal sliding mode controller

articleTitle: Battery State of Health Prediction with Gated Recurrent Neural Networks: A Data-Driven Approach for Battery Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are essential components of stationary energy storage systems, playing a critical role in the harnessing and utilization of renewable energy. Accurately predicting the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is vital for calculating their remaining useful lifetime, which is critical to optimizing the performance of renewable energy systems and increasing reliability and safety. However, achieving this accuracy is challenging, requiring advanced methods. Neural networks offer a solution for predicting the future state of health without requiring a detailed understanding of the battery's internal electrochemical processes. This article presents a deep learning-based approach for SOH prediction using gated recurrent unit-based neural networks. The prediction error is evaluated on a rolling window basis and highlights the importance of data availability. The concept is demonstrated using battery experimental data provided by NASA.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Study on Virtual Reality Applied to Military Training
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In the defense domain, the adoption of Virtual Reality (VR)-based training simulators has significantly increased in recent years in response to the limitations of traditional military training methods. This paper presents a quantitative approach study based on bibliometric metrics to assess the use of VR in defense. Using the Scopus and Web of Science databases as references, the study aimed to identify various aspects related to the research field: distribution of publications, most relevant sources, dynamics of interaction among these sources, prominent topics in recent research, as well as prevalent application areas and supporting technologies. Thus, the study provides valuable insights into the current state and research trends of VR applied to the military context.

articleTitle: Derivation of Weibull Distributions From Spike-like Inputs in Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The idea that artificial neural network based at perceptron can be expressed as a family of Weibull functions is explored. Basically, it is assumed that “spike” inputs produce a kind of deformation on the resulting Sigmoid function or also called activation function. Thus, one would obtain a kind of polynomials so that a relationship to family of polynomials can be well-established. In this paper, it is found that from the fundamental definition of perceptron, the Weibull functions emerge as a family of polynomials that would replace systematically the traditional Sigmoid function. With this, one can conclude that activation function would pass from a binary definition to one continue presumably dictated by distributions of probabilities.

articleTitle: A Study on Improved CartoonGAN with Color Tone Separation White Balancing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Recently, GANs (Generative Adversarial Networks) have rapidly advanced in the field of image style transfer and generation. In particular, CartoonGAN has been the focus of significant research in terms of performance and efficiency for transforming photos into cartoon styles. However, traditional CartoonGANs have limitations in adequately correcting color distortions in the original images, leading to a decline in the quality of the generated images. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel method by applying White Balance preprocessing techniques to CartoonGAN. The proposed method involves classifying images based on the average color temperature of input images with distorted color information, followed by applying White Balance adjustments before feeding the images into CartoonGAN. This study introduces a new approach to improving the performance of GAN models, such as CartoonGAN, in the fields of image processing and computer vision, with potential applications across various domains.

articleTitle: Investigating Young Filipino Farmers' Digital Technology Adoption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Digital technologies are poised to revolutionize agricultural production and address various farm-related issues. However, the current low adoption of these technologies among Filipino farmers is a concern. This paper investigates the reasons behind this and explores the potential for increased adoption among young farmers. The study utilized the Technology Continuance Theory (TCT) - Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) framework, in a quantitative research approach and was validated using structural equation modeling (SEM). The results suggest that technological features, confirmation, satisfaction, and attitude are critical in shaping an individual's attitude, driving to continued adoption. Based on the results of this study, there is a need to raise awareness of the benefits of digital technology by providing farmers' training and educational interventions among young Filipinos.

articleTitle: A Fibonacci-based Switched-Capacitor DC/DC Converter with Dynamically Adjustable Conversion Ratio for Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks offer significant advancement in real-time data collection and analysis in various application scenarios. Sometimes their nodes are placed in difficult-to-reach areas making the replacement of their battery impossible. Therefore, the node is usually equipped with a harvesting system based on PV cells and a lithium-ion battery. A switched-capacitor DC/DC converter is proposed in this paper to optimize the power produced by a single PV cell and maximize the battery charge power. The proposed converter is based on a classic Fibonacci architecture whose control system is improved to make its input/output conversion ratio dynamically adjustable. The simulation results show that the proposed converter allows the usage of more than 90 % of the maximum available PV power to charge the battery of the node. It is important to note that this result is achieved by leveraging the wireless sensor network characteristics to keep the converter as simple as possible.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on a Homogeneous Charge Compression Ignition in Light-Duty Diesel Engine Operated with Commercial Gasoline-Ethanol: in-Cylinder Pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: A pressure sensor was installed in the combustion chamber of a single-cylinder diesel engine that works in HCCI mode (homogeneous charge compression ignition) using gasoline (75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and ethanol (25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) as fuel. The experiments evaluate the pressure and the thermal efficiency of the engine for different temperatures of the air/fuel mixture and for different rotations. The results indicate that the temperature of the mixture had the greatest influence on the start of auto-ignition while the lambda factor had it on the advance of ignition and the release of thermal energy. The engine speed has an influence on the operating range in which the engine can work in HCCI mode, always considering minimum values of the cycle-to-cycle variation (COVPmax). The pressure variation from cycle to cycle decreases with the increase in the equivalence ratio until the detonation zone is reached and an increase in COV values is observed. The maximum pressure peaks increase with lambda and with the mixture temperature since any variation in the fuel injection will have a direct effect on the energy release and therefore on the pressure levels. Finally, rising the temperature of the mixture increases as well the pressure at which the HCCI operation starts.

articleTitle: Oscillations of Modern Synchronous Generators in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The introduction of new energy sources, advancements in storage facilities, and the development of power electronics devices have significantly impacted power systems. These innovations, along with complex control strategies, economical operational practices, and cost-efficient equipment construction, have introduced challenges to small-signal stability, particularly affecting local mode oscillations. Currently, there is a notable absence of comprehensive analyses of local oscillations in contemporary synchronous generators. The scope of this investigation is to analyse local oscillations and their underlying causes to mitigate their adverse effects. The primary objective of the paper is the analysis of several dozen generators within Slovenian power system. Initially, the paper outlines mathematical models suited for studying local oscillations. A significant contribution of this paper lies in the formulation of practical guidelines to assist power plant operators in mitigating stability issues. Additionally, the paper estimates eigenvalue boundaries associated with local modes. To validate these findings, experiments were conducted using laboratory-scale synchronous generators to confirm the conclusions derived from numerical analyses.

articleTitle: Social media emotional state classification prediction based on Arctic Puffin Algorithm (APO) optimization of Transformer mode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper discusses a method to optimize the Transformer model using the Arctic Puffin Optimization Algorithm (APO) for predicting and classifying users' emotional states. The experiment is divided into a main experiment and a comparison experiment. In the main experiment, the APO- optimized Transformer shows significant performance improvement, with the fitness curve stabilizing after two iterations. The model achieved 98.79<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> accuracy on the training set and 98.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on the test set, with the accuracy and loss curves further validating its effectiveness. In the comparison experiment, we compared the proposed method with three basic machine learning models, with the random forest model performing best at 94.7% accuracy. However, the APO-optimized Transformer surpassed the random forest, achieving a 3.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> improvement with 98.10% accuracy. These results demonstrate the potential of the APO algorithm in deep learning and its effectiveness for social media sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Problem Formulation of Portfolio Optimization with Loans and Its Solution by Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm and Convex-Hull Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Portfolio optimization that allows the borrowed money from a loan to be invested in risk assets is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. Then it is proved that the optimal solution of the portfolio optimization problem borrows money up to the limit if it uses the loan. Based on the knowledge, a revised artificial bee colony algorithm using a mapping-based constraint-handling technique is proposed to solve the portfolio optimization problem. The effectiveness of investments with loans is demonstrated by asset data for the Japanese stock market.

articleTitle: Enhancing Public Building Energy Efficiency Through Digital Twin Modeling and Iterative Simulation: A Sustainable Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The digital twin of a public building, Città Metropolitana di Milano, is simulated to analyze energy consumption and efficiency under various operational conditions and assumptions. Iterative simulations identified key measures for reducing energy consumption and enhancing efficiency, focusing on window glazing, reduced lighting power density, and solar panel integration, considering constant HVAC systems and schedules. The analysis compares a base case with existing characteristics to a proposed case incorporating energy-efficient measures, yielding improvements in energy performance. These strategies reduce reliance on fossil fuel-based energy and promote a transition to sustainable energy sources. These performance measures reduce reliance on fossil fuel-based energy consumption and pave the way toward greener and more sustainable energy resources-based energy consumption as per UN SGDs 7 and 11. This research will be a valuable tool for policymakers and building managers to visualize real-time energy performance to ensure improved energy efficiency and predictive maintenance.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Photovoltaic Module Defects based on Infrared images with Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The study presents an innovative approach for detecting defects in photovoltaic modules using deep learning techniques applied to infrared and electroluminescence images. This method offers enhanced accuracy and efficiency over traditional manual inspections by employing advanced algorithms to identify issues like micro-cracks and delamination. The implementation of this technology promises significant improvements in the maintenance and performance of solar energy systems.

articleTitle: Classifying 5G Encrypted Packet Traces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In today's digital era, privacy concerns have raised and the further deployment of 5G technology in recent years has amplified some of these concerns. While encryption is undoubtedly the cornerstone for protecting user privacy, packet trace analysis has been shown to be capable of identifying web and mobile applications even when the network traffic is encrypted. We further extend previous studies by presenting an accurate traffic classifier for 5G packet traces that does not need any access to the network. Our novel classification method is based exclusively on traffic patterns and does not require any information from the network layer to function. We perform a preliminary experimental comparison study for the classification task with three machine learning models and eight popular mobile applications. Our best model reaches an accuracy of up to 87% in classifying one minute of captured 5G encrypted traffic. This prompts us to question if necessary measures need to be considered at the link layer so to alleviate to leak such information.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 3.75 Gbit/s Secure SAC-OCDMA-WDM-FSO System by Using the AND Subtraction Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This study utilized Free-Space Optical (FSO) communication technology to evaluate the feasibility and performance of a highly secure Spectral Amplitude Coding Optical Code Division Multiple Access (SAC-OCDMA) system. The system was combined with FSO technology, offering significant advantages, including large bandwidth, secure data transmission, and license-free operation. The performance of the system was evaluated by several factors, such as transmission range, system capacity, number of channels, and the bit error rate (BER) under various meteorological conditions. Extensive simulations were conducted to examine the impact to evaluate the performance matrix of the proposed network using commercially available Optisystem software. The system architecture employed four channels and utilized a low-cost white light source for data transmission. In optimal clear weather conditions, the system achieved a data rate of 3.75 Gbit/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> across a transmission distance of 9 km while maintaining the specified pre-forward error correction (FEC) bit error rate threshold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(10^{-3})$</tex>. The study also explored system optimization strategies to enhance performance under adverse weather conditions. The system's attributes were compared with recent studies, showcasing superior performance in terms of 6 times data rate approximately and 3 times transmission distance approximately. Additionally, the results provide valuable insights into the potential applications of FSO-based SAC-OCDMA systems, particularly in urban networks, disaster recovery, and military operations, where traditional wired or radio-frequency communication systems may face limitations or vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Formal Algebraic Model of a Generic BCube Data Center Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The optimization of data center performance need to consider different points of view, such as higher bandwidth, lower latency, lower costs, lower energy efficiency, or higher resource capacity. However, the selection of an appropriate data center network architecture is one of the key features as it can make a difference in some of those points. In this paper, a formal algebraic model of a generic BCube is presented ir order to remark the main characteristics of this server-centric approach.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of 2-Elements Printed Inverted-F MIMO Antenna with Step Cavity Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this paper, a 2-elements printed Inverted-F MIMO antenna with step cavity reflector is proposed for Wi- Fi (2.4 GHz-2.5 GHz) and sub 6 GHz 5G (3.6 GHz-4.1 GHz and 4.5 GHz-4.6 GHz) applications. A rectangular element is added to the feeding element of antenna to enhance the impedance bandwidth and decoupling element is installed to improve the isolation between antennas. Moreover, a step cavity reflector is positioned behind the inverted-F MIMO antenna to enhance the gain. The introduced antenna exhibits good impedance matching at 2.4 GHz -2.79 GHz and 3.39 GHz - 4.83 GHz and maintains a required isolation the operational frequency range. The gain exceeds 5 dBi within the frequency ranges of Wi-Fi and Sub 6GHz 5G applications.

articleTitle: Neural Network for the Detection of Fire Ants and Other Invasive Species
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Solenopsis Invicta, also known as fire ant, is a major threat in different locations around the world because of the destructive power it may hold. In order to carry out the early detection of relevant ant hills, a model based on YOLOv8 has been trained and tested in order to recognize them in aerial pictures of the ground, taken by drones. An average detection rate of 87% has been achieved with the current model, even though it is expected to get this figure increased if a larger amount of pictures are used in the training process.

articleTitle: Synapse as a Control System Based at a Thevenin LRC Biocircuit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Synapse as any other nature mechanism aims to optimize processes, in that case is to guarantee the dynamics of neurotransmitters. Since them would acquire the role as electric charges, then one might to assume that synapse might be running exactly as a linear electrical circuit. Under this view, then all laws that determine the electric circuits can be applied well. This paper has as central argument the usage of well-known Thévenin theorem at the proposed RLC circuit, that presumably governs electric interactions at axon terminal. Once the electrical conditions have been established, interestingly axon converts in a device with a behavior of negative feedback control system. This is in accordance to the mechanism by which synaptic vesicles might be releasing neurotransmitters in an opposite direction to adjacent neuron. Negative feedback would yield an inherent equilibrium at the synapse process. In this manner, synapse runs as an self-controlled process that guarantees the pass of neuro-transmitters minimizing fails and optimizing the distribution of neurotransmitters after their releasing from vesicles.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Brain tumor classification and segmentation are crucial medical imaging procedures that aid in diagnosis and treatment planning. This study provides a detailed analysis of the methodologies and techniques used in this subject, which includes conventional machine learning (ML), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), capsule networks (CapsNets), and vision transformers (ViTs). This survey identifies key challenges and opportunities in brain tumor analysis and delineates future research directions. Extant literature predominantly focuses on individual tasks such as tumor detection, segmentation, or grade estimation, indicating the necessity for integrated frameworks capable of simultaneous multi-tasking, particularly with multi-grade classification. While CNNs have been extensively utilized, alternative architectures such as CapsNets and ViTs offer promising avenues for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Study on CartoonGAN Using High-Resolution Generative Networks Through Feature Emphasis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: GAN is a model that generates completely new data and can create various media contents. CartoonGAN is a GAN model that converts real images into cartoon style, and can apply various cartoon styles. In this study, we propose ESRGAN (Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks) technology as a preprocessing method to improve the performance of CartoonGAN. ESRGAN is a model that improves resolution using GAN. This method showed better performance than other SR techniques in the evaluation indices MSE, PSNR, and SSIM results. This suggests that ESRGAN is effective in high-resolution restoration ability and visual quality improvement in cartoon style image conversion. The method proposed in this study can be used as a useful tool for high-resolution cartoon image generation. Since the learning data of the model is limited to a specific domain, there may be limitations in generalizability. Due to the characteristics of ESRGAN, which is computationally complex and consumes a lot of resources, there may be limitations in applying it to real-time processing or large datasets. In future studies, it is necessary to build an extended dataset for various images to overcome these limitations. It is important to reduce computational costs by making models lightweight and optimizing them, and to develop algorithms suitable for real-time processing. It is expected that these additional studies and improvements will be utilized to produce high-quality images.

articleTitle: Dynamic Pickup and Delivery Task Allocation in Multi-Agent Robotic Systems: Vacancy Chain Approaches Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Multi-Agent Robotic Systems (MARS) face the challenge of efficiently dynamic allocating pickup and delivery tasks. Although these tasks are complex and interconnected, many existing research efforts prioritize improving task allocation efficiency while neglecting the critical aspects of overall completion time and load balance in dynamic task allocation scenarios. This gap often results in suboptimal performance, with increased operational delays and inefficiencies. To address this problem, this paper proposes a modified vacancy chain approach with two different strategies: greedy and probability based. These strategies are designed to dynamically optimize task allocation, reducing completion time and balancing the workload among robots. The methods are validated through extensive simulations in the Robot Operating System (ROS) and Gazebo environments. Results demonstrate that while the greedy strategy is highly effective in speed within static settings, the probability-based strategy offers better adaptability and workload distribution in dynamic conditions. These findings could contribute to enhancing the efficiency and responsiveness of multi-robot systems in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Study on Heartbeat and Respiration Rates Estimation with Two Wave Models by using mmWave MIMO FM-CW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In the last decade, remote non-contact monitoring of human vital signs has recently received lots of attention due to the advancement and availability of millimeter wave radars. The research on monitoring of heartbeat and respiration by radar without contact and restraint has been actively conducted. For this purpose, the frequency band uses microwave or millimeter wave and the Doppler radar using CW wave and the frequency modulated continuous wave (FM-CW) radar are utilized. These radar's observation quantities are the Doppler frequency, phase and amplitude of radar signal with respect to a small displacement of chest's skin due to heartbeat and respiration. Therefore, the estimation of heartbeat and respiration rates from radar signal is needed. The various estimation methods have been proposed. A digital filter is difficult to evaluate the heartbeats and respiration rates simultaneously due to the presence of heartbeat harmonics. In this paper, we propose a two-wave models of the small displacement related to respiration and heartbeat, and examines to estimate both rates by phase information of mmWave MIMO FM-CW Radar signal. The heartbeat rate and respiration rate are estimated the phase information of mmWave MIMO FM-CW radar by using two-wave models and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO).

articleTitle: Extended Reality as an Assistive Technology for Patients Suffering from Neurodegenerative Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases with memory impairment and difficulties in recognizing people pose significant challenges to patients' well-being and independence. This research proposes an approach leveraging extended reality (XR) headsets and Computer Vision techniques to enhance person identification for such patients. The system utilizes Unity AR Foundation and OpenCV for real-time face detection and recognition, enabling accurate identification of familiar individuals within the wearer's environment with an immersive AR experience, overlaying digital information next to recognized faces in the wearer's field of view. This research aims to improve social interactions, reduce panic/confusion, and improve overall quality of life for patients with neurodegenerative diseases and represents an advancement in the intersection of healthcare and augmented reality technologies.

articleTitle: Optimizing Mobile Robot Navigation: A Genetic Algorithm and Convolutional Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The Robotics industry can handle optimization issues by utilizing hybrid neural network implementations in conjunction with genetic algorithms. Offline evolution carries out fitness assessments, whereas neural networks are deep learning architectures that handle a variety of classification and regression issues. Although a number of neural networks employ genetic algorithms, none of them were applied with the use of a self-navigating Quanser Qcar mobile robot for dataset generation and validation. In this study, a hybrid strategy is used to optimize hidden layer weights and improve neural network performance through the application of genetic algorithms. Simultaneously, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is developed as a classifier to detect the presence of obstacles and impediments that Quanser Qcar may encounter. This technique constructs a model by randomly selecting the fittest members while supplying a specific number of problem-dependent minimum sub-population sizes. The algorithm includes crossover, mutation, encoding, and selection to determine the global optimum and enable the mobile car to avoid obstacles.

articleTitle: Leveraging Extravagant Linguistic Patterns to Enhance Fake Review Detection: A Comparative Study on Clustering Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Online reviews are crucial in shaping consumer behavior and business success, but the growing presence of fake reviews threatens the credibility of these platforms. This paper introduces a novel approach to fake review detection by focusing on the use of extravagant language words that are excessively positive or negative, often used to manipulate opinions. We explore how extravagant words can serve as strong indicators of review authenticity. By leveraging advanced clustering methods and BERT embeddings for linguistic feature extraction, we examine patterns in deceptive and genuine reviews. Two diverse datasets are utilized to validate our approach, and the model's performance is evaluated through accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of extravagant words in enhancing the detection of fake reviews and provide valuable insights into improving the reliability of online review systems. This approach offers practical implications for boosting consumer trust and enhancing the integrity of digital platforms.

articleTitle: What's the Key Environment Information that Makes the Blockage Prediction Work?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: To meet the increased communication performance requirements defined in sixth-generation (6G) networks, out-of-band methods are gaining more attention from researchers. These methods consider adding extra information, such as sensing environmental data, to enhance performance. In this context, image-based physical environment blockage prediction methods have been proposed to avoid fast signal attenuation, particularly in millimeter wave (mmWave) bands. However, image data is high-dimensional and requires specialized hardware for fast processing. This paper proposes a real-time blockage prediction method that utilizes images containing only propagation-related foreground information. The method predicts two blockage states using a convolution-based machine learning (ML) approach. We evaluate the proposed method using real-world communication data from a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) scenario. A comparative experiment is conducted to compare the performance of using complete images versus foreground-only images. The neural net-work's max pooling layer is configured with different parameters to test and analyze the impact of non-foreground information. The results show that the foreground-only image-based prediction is more robust for detail extraction and requires less prediction time. As the pooling stride increases, the accuracy of the complete image-based prediction method decreases, while the proposed method maintains high accuracy. Moreover, the proposed can save about 30 % of the prediction time.

articleTitle: Creation and Annotation of a Handwritten Text Database for the Kazakh Language: Methodologies and Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper describes the creation and development of a handwritten text database for the Kazakh language, which aims to overcome the lack of publicly available datasets in this sector. While multiple databases exist for handwritten text recognition in other languages, such as IAM for English and RIMES for French, there is no equivalent resource for Kazakh, which employs the Cyrillic alphabet with additional unique characters. This paper explains the systematic process of creating a handwritten Kazakh text library, from gathering data from over 120 writers to annotating text with technologies such as LabelMe. The collection includes 42 Kazakh alphabet letters and more than 75,000 handwritten characters. By introducing this new dataset, we hope to improve research in optical character recognition (OCR) for the Kazakh language and provide the groundwork for future growth in computer vision and text recognition.

articleTitle: Quantization of Energies with Machine Learning Without Quantum Mechanics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The field of Machine Learning through the technique of artificial neural network is used to determine in a straightforward manner the quantized energies of a particle in an infinite well. To accomplish this, unphysical mathematical assumptions have been applied. In essence, the opted method in this study aims to derive quantization without any knowledge of quantum mechanics of system. Moreover, the Schrödlnger equation has been reconstructed from the information of quantization derived from the usage of neural network. This procedure, although rather artificial might be exploited to derive other quantum mechanics equations without any knowledge to priori of system under study.

articleTitle: A Wireless Wearable System to Monitor Posture when Using Ergonomic Setups
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Ergonomic office setups are often used to prevent chronic pain caused by sitting at a desk for long periods of time. However, these setups are only effective if used correctly. This paper explores a solution that identifies poor posture in the three areas of the body. More ergonomic work office strategies include movements, such as transitioning from sitting to standing and vice versa. A user of this kind of system may need to monitor their posture for different setups. Previous studies have looked at monitoring human activities and static posture. However, most research focuses on one typical setup. The solution in this paper can be applied to three different ergonomic setups - a standing desk, a kneeling chair, and a typical office chair. The system consists of a wearable device, a stationary computer, and a simple user interface. The wearable device has accelerometers that monitor posture points on the upper legs, the torso, the shoulders, and the head. The data is sent wireless to be processed using a machine learning decision tree model. The result of the processed data is shown to the user in real-time. The result corresponds with a picture that helps the user visualize the posture issue detected. Five decision tree models were developed with at least 92 % accuracy. For each ergonomic setup, for each of the three sections of the body monitored, a model would be needed to be developed, resulting in nine different models. However, some of the body positions share similar posture positions across the three ergonomic setups. Reducing the number of models required less training data to be collected. This reduction did not seem to impact the accuracy of the models negatively.

articleTitle: Classification of Lumpy Skin Disease for Cows According to Appropriate Parameter Values in Transfer Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The disease known by different names such as Nodular Exanthema, Cowpox, Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) and African disease in cow is a viral disease transmitted by mosquitoes, ticks and biting flies, which sometimes results in death and lumpy swellings on the skin and internal organs. Since the disease causes serious productivity losses and even deaths in cows, automatic detection methods with computer-aided systems are becoming important. Among the advanced computer-aided methods, diagnosis using deep learning methods is very important for the health of cattle. This study consists of two stages. In the first stage, the aim is to classify the disease on whole/partial digital images of cows using transfer learning (MobileNet, ResNet and Xception) methods and to determine whether the cows detected as diseased are actually diseased. In this stage, the dataset for each method is divided into different training, test and validation parts and the classification success is measured according to different parameters and different evaluation criteria. In the second stage, the performances of the methods are presented comparatively with different evaluation criteria. The complexity matrices and classification accuracies (train, test and valid) for all models are presented separately.

articleTitle: Order Picking Framework for Storage Location of Chemical Warehouse
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Efficient warehouse management is essential for ensuring customer satisfaction. Addressing waiting waste and minimizing working waste is crucial for quality management. This paper presents an order-picking framework aimed at minimizing working time. The framework comprises three key steps: problem identification, model selection, and process simulation. Problem identification involves analyzing the framework concept and root causes, proposed models aim to forecast the number of customer orders, and process simulation helps in finding optimal solutions. The results demonstrate that the proposed model reduced working time by 31.73%. This methodical approach can assist warehouse planners in selecting the best model, thereby supporting effective workforce planning, and enhancing customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: First Demonstration of Fixed Access Network Security Traffic Cleaning Architecture and Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Fixed access network technology can provide high-bandwidth, low-latency, and mass connections for multiple network applications and IoT devices. However, the network services are vulnerable to cyber-attacks. In our demonstration, the proposed traffic cleaning architecture and method with fixed access network slicing technology can offload network traffic flexibly. Its security defense is close to the terminal, which makes enterprise users to be more trust in information robustness. And there is no need to worry about any complications like configurations and connections of information security equipment. All network traffic can be processed at the central office for information security protection.

articleTitle: Leveraging Large Language Models to Enhance Personalized Recommendations in E-commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This study deeply explores the application of large language model (LLM) in personalized recommendation system of e-commerce. Aiming at the limitations of traditional recommendation algorithms in processing large-scale and multi-dimensional data, a recommendation system framework based on LLM is proposed. Through comparative experiments, the recommendation model based on LLM shows significant improvement in multiple key indicators such as precision, recall, F1 score, average click-through rate (CTR) and recommendation diversity. Specifically, the precision of the LLM model is improved from 0.75 to 0.82, the recall rate is increased from 0.68 to 0.77, the F1 score is increased from 0.71 to 0.79, the CTR is increased from 0.56 to 0.63, and the recommendation diversity is increased by 41.2%, from 0.34 to 0.48. LLM effectively captures the implicit needs of users through deep semantic understanding of user comments and product description data, and combines contextual data for dynamic recommendation to generate more accurate and diverse results. The study shows that LLM has significant advantages in the field of personalized recommendation, can improve user experience and promote platform sales growth, and provides strong theoretical and practical support for personalized recommendation technology in e-commerce.

articleTitle: Effect of Transmission Range and Grid Dimensions on Route Cost in WSN Using TABU Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The objective of this work is establish effect of grid size of wireless sensor network and transmission range on the cost incurred by a TABU search algorithm. The simulation work showed that as the area enclosed the WSN nodes increases, so does the cost of transferring data between nodes as a function of routes, and this will definitely affect energy and transmission power. Also, the work shoed that as the transmission range decreases, the cost increases. Thus, the grid dimension and transmission range work in an opposite manner. Both will affect routing cost used by the TABU search algorithm. The work also established a power relationship between grid dimensions and average cost, which helps in optimizing WSN geometrical design. The work also established a mathematical expression relating cost to WSN nodes count.

articleTitle: Using AI and Digital Simulations to Expedite the Learning and Programming of COBOTS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The significant time it takes from authorizing the purchase of a collaborative robot to its installation, including the execution of the purchase order, delivery, and training, results in a considerable wait for users to utilize the robot's potential. This work presents alternatives to reducing the time to use the robot before it arrives at the user's facilities. These tools combine digital simulation and Artificial Intelligence, such as Prompt Engineering. Simulations familiarize users with the robot's configuration and movements, and artificial intelligence is used to learn how to program it. Among the results, it was found that using this combination of tools, users could start programming the collaborative robot from the first day its installation was completed and become utterly familiar with its capabilities. The steps necessary to replicate the efficient learning methodology are shared upon completing this work. This will enable users to become proficient in quickly using and programming the collaborative robot.

articleTitle: Exploring Dialogue Capabilities with Automation Systems in the AAM Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) is the result of advanced technology and requires the ongoing development of autonomous flying and traffic management automation. Applying the analog reporting systems of traditional aviation to AAM would pose significant challenges in achieving efficiency and profitability. The reason for this is because AAM operations necessitate a significant number of personnel, specific training, adaptability to urban environmental changes, and the ability to handle frequent operations. This research aims to tackle these problems by presenting a hybrid automation solution specifically tailored to overcome them. The automation system consists of a safety-focused inference engine designed to adhere to laws and avoid the spread of incorrect information. Additionally, it includes a natural language processing-based dialogue interface designed for diverse stakeholders in the AAM ecosystem. This system aims to investigate the possibility of automating AAM procedures. Proposed future user experiments aim to evaluate enhancements in time and labor efficiency, along with error reduction, with the objective of formulating a comprehensive automation approach for AAM operations. Keywords—Dialogue Interfaces, User-Centered Design, Stakeholder Interaction

articleTitle: Integration of Mamba and Transformer - MAT for Long-Short Range Time Series Forecasting with Application to Weather Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Long-short range time series forecasting is essential for predicting future trends and patterns over extended periods. While deep learning models such as Transformers have made significant strides in advancing time series forecasting, they often encounter difficulties in capturing long-term dependencies and effectively managing sparse semantic features. The state space model, Mamba, addresses these issues through its adept handling of selective input and parallel computing, striking a balance between computational efficiency and prediction accuracy. This article examines the advantages and disadvantages of both Mamba and Transformer models, and introduces a combined approach, MAT, which leverages the strengths of each model to capture unique long-short range dependencies and inherent evolutionary patterns in multivariate time series. Specifically, MAT harnesses the long-range dependency capabilities of Mamba and the short-range characteristics of Transformers. Experimental results on benchmark weather datasets demonstrate that MAT outperforms existing comparable methods in terms of prediction accuracy, scalability, and memory efficiency.

articleTitle: Improved Image Feature Extraction Based on Quantum Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Quantum computing has proliferated by offering the potential for significant exponential speed improvements. Quantum computing potential can be exploited in various fields, such as complex collision image processing in traffic surveillance. Quantum-based computing performs data processing through the principles of quantum mechanisms such as superposition and entanglement. Quantum computing has various applications, including deep learning. The convolution process in deep learning methods can be modified using quantum circuit mechanisms and promises to increase the efficiency of feature extraction compared to classical methods. This paper explains the concept of quantum convolution by exploring two main mechanisms, i.e., entire quantum circuits for convolution and quantum circuits as quantum kernels. We also propose a new quantum circuit that can represent the convolution process. Theoretically, quantum convolution is faster than classical computation. Our results advance knowledge and provide new insights into developing better convolution for feature extraction.

articleTitle: Energy Characterization of an All-Terrain Vehicle with an Internal Combustion Engine Converted to an Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The objective of this study is to analyze the energy efficiency and autonomy delivered by a quad-bike all-terrain vehicle (ATV) with an internal combustion engine and another vehicle with these characteristics converted to an electric vehicle. For the electric vehicle the parameters were collected with a power quality analyzer and a data acquisition system. Both vehicles were tested for measurement of torque and rotation of the drive axle with a torque and rotation sensor implemented on a test bench (chassis dynamometer). The tests were carried out both in the laboratory and in the field, measuring energy parameters that define the efficiency and autonomy of operation. The results indicate that the quad-bike ATV that uses an internal combustion engine converted to an electric vehicle considerably improves efficiency and autonomy. The acceleration capacity of the electric vehicle is considerably greater, the autonomy of the stored fuel represents the same capacity when compared to the storage in the battery, maintaining the same weight of the vehicle. Without considering environmental improvements, the conversion of these low-power vehicles represents an important performance improvement for users and the environment.

articleTitle: Integrating PRINCE2 and Agile Methodologies in Software Development: Unveiling Opportunities and Addressing Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Modern software development now necessitates combining various project management approaches to tackle the fast speed of technical advancements and intricate project demands. This study examines the possibilities and obstacles of integration. Utilising PRINCE2 and Agile methodologies in software development projects. The research emphasises PRINCE2's strong governance and structured procedures, as well as Agile's adaptability and reactivity to change, especially in cultural contexts. Combining PRINCE2's control mechanisms with Agile's flexibility can improve project management by solving cultural difficulties found in agile transitions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Short-Term Load Forecasting Accuracy in the Power Systems Using a Hybrid CNN-GRU Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In modern power systems, Short-Term Load Forecasting (STLF) is critical in ensuring the dynamic allocation of operational reserves and accurate prediction of electrical load demand. STLF is pertinent to grid operators to ensure system stability, allocate generation resources efficiently, and provide adequate reserves to deal with unexpected fluctuations. Considering the pivotal role of STLF, this paper introduces a hybrid deep learning model for short-term load forecasting, combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). The model features two parallel 32-filter convolutional layers (3×3 kernel, ReLU) for spatial feature extraction, followed by two series-connected GRU layers (42 units) to capture temporal dependencies. A final dense layer with ReLU activation generates the load forecast. This architecture effectively leverages CNNs for local pattern recognition and GRUs for modeling temporal sequences, offering a robust solution for accurate short-term load forecasting. Therefore, the efficacy of the CNN-GRU model is tested and validated using an extensive dataset sourced from the National Transmission & Dispatch Company (NTDC), Pakistan. The performance analysis reveals that hybrid CNN-GRU models achieve a substantial reduction in Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), with values of 400.33, 2.89, 580.95, for single-step forecasts, respectively, and 1031.11, 5.31, and 733.19, for 24-hour forecasts. Furthermore, the simulation results demonstrate notable enhancements in load forecasting accuracy and robustness across various forecast horizons.

articleTitle: Multi-View Human Activity Recognition in Ambient Assisted Living Using Lightweight Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) is crucial for the development of intelligent assistive technologies in Ambient Assisted Living (AAL) environments. This paper proposes an innovative method for Multi-View Human Activity Recognition (MV-HAR) using lightweight deep learning models, specifically MobileNet and Cyclone-CNN (CCNet), to achieve quick and precise activity detection. Utilizing the Robot House Multi-View Human Activity Recognition (RHM-HAR) dataset, which contains four different views-front, back, ceiling (omni), and mobile robot-our models effectively address challenges related to viewpoint variation and motion dynamics. The dataset includes 14 multi-view daily living action classes, providing a balanced set of synchronized human actions suitable for multi-domain neural network learning. MobileNet and CCNet are employed for their high recognition accuracy, computational efficiency, and real-time application capabilities in AAL scenarios. We propose a Mutual Information (MI)-based method to assess the redundancy and relevance of each viewpoint, ensuring the fusion of multi-view data with minimum redundancy and maximum relevance. Benchmarking results demonstrate that multi-view combinations significantly enhance recognition performance compared to single-view models, particularly in complex activities involving high levels of movement.

articleTitle: Intelligent Marine Debris Cleaning Robot: A Solution to Ocean Pollution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Facing the growing global problem of marine pollution, many different types of marine debris removal robots have been developed. However, there are still many improvements that can be made among them. In this paper, we propose a device that can automatically collect and target marine debris, in addition to utilizing the abundance of solar energy available. In this design, the efficiency of ocean cleanup is greatly improved by utilizing ultrasonic, pressure and GPS sensors. Making excellent contribution to global sustainable development.

articleTitle: TechnoSearch: Improving e-Commerce Searches Using Product Category and Brand Based Ranking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Search in e-commerce websites is a search-engine based technology that allows customers to find desired products based on keywords related to the items. The product search function should be designed to not only present the products that customers are looking for but also offer suitable alternatives, thereby providing more choices for customers. Consequently, the effectiveness of product searches is evaluated by their impact on increasing product visibility and the number of purchases. Well-known metrics used to measure search effectiveness include Click Rate, Cart Add Rate, and Order Rate. By improving these metrics, search can play a significant role in boosting website sales. In this article, we focus on specific features of product information to enhance these metrics in search and present an algorithm called TechnoSearch. The TechnoSearch algorithm identifies the categories and brands preferred by customers, providing more relevant product options in response to customer searches. As a result, we have achieved an average increase of approximately 18% in Click Rate by expanding the number of suitable choices for customers.

articleTitle: Faulty Sensors Detection in Planar Array Antenna Using Fish School Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Antenna arrays are integral to high-performance systems such as radar, wireless communications, satellite communications, radio astronomy, and medical imaging. However, sensor failure within PAA can severely affect the radiation pattern, which may cause signal gain reduction and compromised directionality, especially when central elements are not working. This paper presents a new approach in antenna arrays for detecting faulty sensors using the Fish School Search Algorithm (FSSA). The detection problem is framed as an optimization of the Mean Square Error (MSE) between the expected and actual radiation patterns for single and multiple elements faults, enabling early identification of these faults. Simulations on both 3x3 and 9x9 planar arrays are performed to evaluate the method's accuracy, considering different fault scenarios, including central and edge element failures. Simulation results show that FSSA accurately detects faulty sensors, with central element failures having a significant impact on system performance. The proposed method enhances system reliability by detecting faults promptly and minimizing performance downtime in critical applications.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Consequences of Data Breaches: Risks, Impacts, and Mitigation in the Digital Age
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In an increasingly interconnected digital world, data breaches have become a critical challenge affecting individuals, organizations, and society.
