This research paper delves into the critical issue of data breaches in the digital era, where data has become a vital part of both businesses and individuals. We explored the causes, impacts, and aftermath of data breaches, and then highlighted the significant risks these data breaches pose to individuals, organizations, and society. The paper serves as a comprehensive guide to understanding data breaches and offers insights into building a safer and more secure digital future for all. Data breach occurs when unauthorized individuals gain access to sensitive or confidential information, resulting in its exposure, theft, or misuse. Data breaches are large-scale corporate businesses or individual privacy violations, the significance of these attacks disrupt public trust, compromise sensitive information, and disrupt digital ecosystems around the world. This paper finally examines the ramifications of data breaches, such as financial loss, identity theft, reputational damage, and emotional/psychological distress. We then investigated the fate of stolen data, discussing its use in dark web marketplaces, credential stuffing attacks, identity theft, financial fraud, and reputational damage.

articleTitle: Design Options for Thermal Uprate of a Transmission Line: A Case Study in the South African Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Due to the exponential increase in electricity demand driven by increase in economic activities, the electrical infrastructure operation will be impacted due to the need to transmit more power to the end users. Although the existing electrical infrastructure is designed to accommodate more additional capacity, some of the transmission lines will be operating closer to their thermal capacity limits. This can cause adverse system challenges if it is not addressed in the form of building additional electrical lines that will accommodate and transmit more capacity will be planned to be introduced within the power system. However, capital constraints, servitude or right of way (RoW) acquisition, line construction duration and other legislative requirements pose a significant stumbling block in building of new lines. The utilisation of the existing lines and recycling servitude in transmitting more power remains an attractive option, provided it is carefully planned and designed. However, the process of planning and designing for capacity uprating of lines is not systematically outlined for ease of implementation. The aim of this study is that of documenting and demonstrating the systematic process to be followed when considering the uprating of an existing line considering various options that can be implemented. The results demonstrate the capacity achieved including the benefits derived within the South African power system.

articleTitle: Fake Review Detection Using Extravagant Words: A Comparative Study of K-means, K-mode, and Hierarchical Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In the digital age, online reviews playa critical role in influencing consumer decisions and business reputations. How-ever, the prevalence of fake reviews undermines the credibility of online platforms. In this study, we propose a new method based on the use of extravagant words as indicators of fake reviews, leveraging their tendency to exaggerate and manipulate readers. We aim to evaluate the effectiveness of this approach by comparing three distinct methods: K-means, K-mode, and Hierarchical clustering. Utilizing two comprehensive datasets, we preprocess the data, extract features, and implement the tree classification methods. Additionally, we incorporate BERT for improved feature extraction. The performance of each method is assessed using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score. Our findings reveal significant insights into the utility of extravagant words and BERT in distinguishing fake reviews and highlight the comparative strengths and weaknesses of K-means, K-modes and Hierarchical clustering. This study provides a novel approach to enhance review authenticity verification, with implications for improving consumer trust and platform integrity.

articleTitle: Simulations of Non-Invasive Vehicle Wheel Faults Detection using AI-driven Motor Surrogate Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper experiments with fault detection of vehicle wheels by using a surrogate model of an AC motor, sensors, and AI tools. The surrogate model is explored in this paper to simulate the moving vehicle with wheel faults and examine the effects with a non-invasive method. This non-invasive method provides the benefits of not requiring modification to the operational system, fewer costs, and issues, and no downtime, and the surrogate model would allow us to experiment with the referred effects of rotational faults on a vehicle wheel without possible safety issues on the road. For the motor experiment setup, the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensor is installed on the motor to collect the vibration data, and a microphone is used to collect the audio data. Four different rotational faults and disturbances are inflicted on the motor in operation and the effect data collected to be analyzed. Faults are unbalanced faults, bearing faults, load faults, and mounting faults. These fault data from the motor system are collected, computed, and translated into inferred data for the vehicle wheel. For example, the mounting fault data collected on the rotating motor is inferred as data from a rotating vehicle wheel with mounting issues, such as missing lug nuts. Also, the collected vibration data is used to infer the effects on audio and vehicle speed, such as vehicle speed performance degrading with increased vibration due to wheel vibrating and wobbling. And increase of decibels due to higher vibration magnitude values. The audio data from the microphone, vibration data from IMU, and Instrument Panel (IP) with Revolutions Per Minute (RPM) and speed gauges are analyzed by AI network tools. The experiment results show that the features and patterns collected from the devices used for training, and decision-making Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) were able to correctly classify the fault as “D” Mounting Fault with a likelihood value of 50%.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Cloud Service Models: IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS in the Context of Emerging Technologies and Trend
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Cloud computing has become a pivotal technology in modern IT infrastructures, offering scalable, on-demand resources across various service models: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS). This paper comprehensively reviews these service models, highlighting their key functionalities, major providers, and specific use cases. Through a comparative analysis, we examine the differences in management, cost implications, scalability, and user control, providing insights into the advantages and disadvantages of each model from both provider and user perspectives. Furthermore, the paper discusses emerging technologies such as AI, machine learning, and edge computing and their impact on cloud service models. Recent market trends, security concerns, and compliance developments are explored to illustrate the growing importance of secure cloud adoption. Finally, real-world case studies are presented, showcasing successful implementations of IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS and the lessons learned from these examples. The paper concludes by addressing challenges like data privacy, vendor lock-in, and interoperability while offering predictions on the future evolution of cloud service models and potential innovations.

articleTitle: Acorn 4.0: An Platform Auxilied by AI for Acorn Value Chain Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This work illustrates the initial results obtained within the scope of the WebLand project, presenting the needs, industrial factors and methodology used in the development of a digital solution aimed at the bolota trade in Portugal, valuing the value chain of this abundant product. The project envisages the development of a marketplace platform that allows tracking national acorn production, predicting supply and searching, as well as assisting in choosing logistical routes for transporting this material. The platform's functionalities are supported by artificial intelligence algorithms for analyzing complex data and dynamic routes considering conditioning factors in the process of purchasing and using this product and by-products through convulational models. The data collection, its normalization and characterization in relation to the different ones are specific results of the initial activities, also presented in this work, which support the implementation of the data model in the concept of valuing acorns as an option to conventional products. The proposed solution within the scope of this project foresees and idealizes assistance in making logistical decisions with the intention of reducing the desperation of agricultural production, quickly connecting classes in the value chain and reducing the environmental footprint associated with acorns.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Network-Based Semi-Addressable Fire Detection and Alarm System with Zone Loop Short and Open Circuit Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Fire detection and alarm systems (FDAS) play a vital role in the early detection and warning in the event of a fire. The choice of the FDAS type installation is highly dependent on the requirements of the building as determined by the design professional. This research focused on the design and implementation of a semi-addressable FDAS that uses conventional FDAS components. It uses Arduino Uno for control and processing, XBee S2C RF modules using the DigiMesh protocol for the wireless network structure, INA226 sensing module to monitor the loop current. The system's different parameters were validated in the different tests. As the distance between nodes increased, the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) in dBm became more negative and the RSSI pulse became narrower. The throughput was nearly constant as the distance between nodes increases for both line of sight (LOS) and non-line of sight (NLOS) conditions. The round-trip time (RTT) was also nearly constant under LOS condition while non-constant for NLOS condition. The analysis of variance (ANOVA) test suggests that the number of payload bytes has an influence on the RSSI pulses and the RSSI values (dBm) has an influence on the RTT values (ms) for both LOS and NLOS conditions.

articleTitle: PlatePal: A Comprehensive Image-Based Food Analysis and Dietary Assistant Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This study presents a mobile food journaling application which offers functionalities to help users become aware of nutritional content and calories consumed throughout the day. We focus on composite cuisine, particularly Thai food, which comprises mixed ingredients, thus posing a challenge in recognizing and identifying combined components. Underlying techniques of the application are based on machine learning, aiming to perform three main tasks: (1) food classification, (2) volume estimation, and (3) chatbot functionality that offers dietary advice and consultations to improve the user experience. This study conducted extensive experiments to identify models that achieve the best performance for each task. The results indicate that Xception outperformed other models in both food classification and image segmentation. For volume estimation, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) demonstrated the ability to capture efficient depth perception, which was utilized by MiDas to generate a Point Cloud that approximates the volume of an input food image. For the chatbot, this study adopts OpenAI's GPT-3.5-turbo model, fine-tuned with nutritional data from the Department of Health of Thailand. The results show that the system is capable of delivering accurate responses. Finally, PlatePal received an overall evaluation of 8.53 out of 10, reflecting a high level of user satisfaction. This initiative is designed to promote healthier eating habits and contribute to the well-being of the Thai population across all age groups.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Risk Management Frameworks on IT Audits: A Comparative Analysis of COSO, COBIT, ISO/IEC 27001, and NIST CSF
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In today's digital landscape, information technology (IT) audits are critical for ensuring an in digital landscape nowadays. Frameworks related to risk management provide a systematic approach to identify and reduce IT risks. Control frameworks provide a defined method for analyzing internal controls and ensuring the effectiveness of IT audits. This study focuses on the impact and effectiveness of four major frameworks on IT audits: COSO, COBIT, ISO/IEC 27001, and NIST CSF. We investigate how each framework organizes the audit process, aids in control gap discovery, improves audit efficiency, and allows for unambiguous reporting. In addition, we explain factors to consider while picking the best framework for an organization's specific risk profile. The study conducts a thorough assessment of their strengths, shortcomings, and applicability for various IT audit scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Medical Summarization with Parameter Efficient Fine Tuning on Local CPUs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Documenting and summarizing patient symptoms and medical history for each visit can significantly burden clinicians' time management. Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated great potential in natural language processing (NLP) tasks; however, their effectiveness in clinical summarization tasks has not yet been rigorously validated. While much research has focused on leveraging closed LLMs like GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini for clinical applications, privacy concerns hinder their deployment in real clinical settings. On-premises deployment offers a potential solution. This study examines domain adaptation techniques on the open-source LLM, Llama 3 8B Instruct, to improve clinical summarization. Our approach emphasizes fine-tuning on CPUs instead of the more commonly used GPU s, aiming for greater cost savings in practical applications. We apply Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) for efficient task-specific adaptation and introduce CPU optimization techniques such as IPEX-LLM and Intel® AMX to enhance performance. Our results show that CPU fine-tuning provides a practical, cost-effective, and privacy-aware alternative to GPU fine-tuning, while improving the accuracy of medical summarization and enabling customization to meet unique clinical requirements.

articleTitle: Implementation of Li-Fi Technology in Smart Classrooms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This study presents a unique approach to Li-Fi, or Light Fidelity technology, becoming integrated into smart classrooms by offering a faster and more secure method of exchanging data rather than the traditional Wi-Fi. Data is transmitted wirelessly via light waves so that electromagnetic interference is negligible and should, therefore, improve data transfer efficiency. At the heart of this system is the Raspberry Pi, an affordable microcontroller that manages the exchange of data between the LED light source and the receiving device. At high speed, the modulated LED provides fast multi-media, educational material and real-time communication. This helps in more quick and reliable sources of access to bettering classroom learning. The paper goes into such technical details in the Li- Fi system setup about transmitters and receivers with the involvement of Raspberry Pi in the network. The key contribution lies in a solution to improving data distribution and connectivity within an educational environment in an affordable and scalable manner, thereby enhancing the richness of learning environments for students.

articleTitle: Hybrid PSOCSA-Driven Power Allocation for Capacity and Spectral Efficiency Optimization in Spatially Correlated MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid opti-mization framework for maximizing the capacity and spectral efficiency of MIMO systems with spatially correlated antennas under Rayleigh fading channels. The system model incorporates Doppler shift to account for mobility and applies a power allocation scheme optimized using a Hybrid Particle Swarm Opti-mization and Chameleon Swarm Algorithm (PSOCSA). Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) is employed to efficiently decompose the MIMO channel into independent sub-channels, with power allocated to maximize the system capacity. Detailed mathematical formulations of the channel capacity, incorporating both antenna correlation and Doppler effects, are provided. Comparative analysis demonstrates that the proposed PSOCSA algorithm significantly outperforms other state-of-the-art algorithms, such as Whale Optimization(WOA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Chameleon Swarm Algorithm (CSA), Harris Hawks Op-timization (HHO), and Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA) in terms of both computational efficiency and capacity maximization across various MIMO configurations (4×4, 8×8, 16×16, 64×64). Our results indicate that PSOCSA achieves superior performance with the lowest computational time and higher stability, making it a promising approach for real-time optimization and enhancement of the efficiency of MIMO systems in next-generation wireless networks.

articleTitle: Time Series and Machine Learning Methods for Short-Term Load Forecasting in Modern Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Accurate load forecasting is crucial for modern power systems but faces challenges like data scarcity, tool limitations, and lack of institutional support. Inaccurate forecasts lead to resource inefficiency and inadequate electricity supply. This paper compares time series and machine learning methods for short-term load forecasting. Time series analysis uses statistical techniques to predict future values from past data, identifying trends and cycles. Machine learning algorithms, including neural networks, support vector machines, and decision trees, handle large, non-linear data relationships and improve with more data. The meta-analysis thoroughly assesses these approaches by examining multiple studies and considering aspects such as prediction performance, computational complexity, data demands, and flexibility. The detailed comparison will help the researchers understand each method's merits and demerits. Thus, knowing these details, the researchers can easily select the most appropriate forecasting model for the given problem, contributing to the enhancement of load forecasting in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Homogeneous Charge Compression Ignition in a Light-duty Diesel Engine Operated with Commercial Gasoline-ethanol
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: An experimental bench was designed and developed to carry out experimental tests of a Diesel cycle engine using gasoline as fuel. The engine (originally a diesel cycle) was fitted with different devices to run in HCCI mode. These modifications did not affect the engine's original condition, which can be returned to diesel mode at any time. Instrumentation was set up to measurement the temperature (exhaust gases, inlet charge inlet, lubricating oil), pressure (intake air, gasoline inlet, combustion chamber), torque, rpm, air flow and fuel flow. The engine was subjected to different operating conditions and control parameters to study and analyze the effects of engine speed, air-fuel ratio and mixture temperature (air-gasoline). The results indicate that higher temperatures or amounts of fuel cause an earlier ignition phase, which would have a direct influence on the beginning of combustion. The results also indicate that, by increasing the amount of fuel and varying the inlet temperature, more useful energy is generated until reaching the limit of the detonation zone. Small gains in combustion efficiency translate into significant energy savings, also reducing exhaust gas pollution levels.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Pre-Trained Object Detection Models: Performance, Efficiency, and Application Suitabilit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This study conducts a detailed comparative evaluation of pre-trained object detection models in TensorFlow, including SSD, EfficientDet, RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, and YOLOv4. Performance metrics such as accuracy, inference time, frames per second (FPS), and memory utilization were assessed using the COCO and Pascal VOC datasets. The results indicate that SSD provides a balanced trade-off between speed and accuracy, making it suitable for scenarios requiring moderate performance. EfficientDet demonstrates superior resource efficiency while achieving the highest accuracy, positioning it as the most appropriate model for applications requiring high accuracy and resource optimization. RetinaNet, although slower, excels in detecting small objects, offering advantages in precision for intricate object detection tasks. Faster R-CNN outperforms other models in handling complex, cluttered images but at the cost of real-time performance. YOLOv4, despite challenges in handling overlapping and small objects, delivers the fastest inference time, making it highly effective for real-time applications. This comparative analysis underscores each model's distinct advantages and limitations, providing insights into their suitability based on specific operational requirements.

articleTitle: Integrating Optimization Techniques in Software Development Life Cycle - SLR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The software development life cycle (SDLC) is a structured process for delivering a high-quality product within a specified timeframe. Developing a cost-effective and efficient software product life cycle has always been a priority in software engineering, which can impact product quality. This study aims to provide an overview of the recent articles that focus on applying optimization techniques, mathematical models, and software cost estimation in the software development process and propose possible future directions. For the selected 29 studies, the development phase of the SDLC is most commonly focused on in studies. This emphasis highlights the pivotal role of optimization and mathematical modeling in enhancing software development efficiency.

articleTitle: Development of a CNN Approach Classification Model for Soybean (Glycine max., L.) and its Common Weeds to Support Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Weeds significantly interfere with soybean production, leading to an 84% reduction in yield when uncontrolled. This study explores the application of the YOLOv8 deep learning algorithm for the effective identification and classification of soybean crops and common weeds, particularly focusing on the CLSoy 1 variety. By utilizing a low-cost 1080p webcam, images of soybeans and weeds were captured for analysis. The research implemented machine vision and image processing techniques to enhance weed management strategies, thus minimizing the reliance on chemical herbicides and addressing ecological concerns. A comprehensive dataset of 523 annotated images was processed using YOLOv8, resulting an accuracy of 83% and a precision of 88%. The Intersection over Union (IoU) score of 0.71 indicates a satisfactory overlap between predicted and actual results, although the mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.48 recommends areas for improvement. The key findings highlight the potential of integrating advanced technologies in precision agriculture, underscoring the need for sustainable and efficient weed management solutions. Future work will aim to enhance detection capabilities, possibly with higher-quality imaging equipment and advanced data augmentation techniques, to further improve the model's performance in diverse agricultural environments.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Robot-Student Interaction (RSI) in Laboratory Teaching
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Through the assistance of teachers and increased student participation, this study introduced a teaching assistant robot to improve laboratory education. The robot used cutting-edge technology like real-time navigation, sensor and actuator detection, voice command recognition, and pneumatic symbol identification. Omnidirectional mobility was made possible using Mecanum wheels, and obstacle avoidance and path planning were optimized by the A* algorithm. Detailed maps were created using LiDAR and a SLAM technique to enable seamless navigation in challenging situations. The robot's CNN models and YOLO enabled intuitive interaction by recognizing voice commands and symbols. It accomplished 90.4 % overall accuracy, 90.1 % path efficiency, 84.1 % performance in pneumatic symbol, sensors, and actuator recognition, and 91.2 % speech recognition accuracy. These findings demonstrated how the robot may use state-of-the-art navigation and interface technologies in lab environments to improve student engagement and educator support.

articleTitle: Sign Language Recognition using PCA and Hu-Moment Features
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The deaf community commonly uses sign language for communication, a highly flexible way of conveying messages. Sign language involves a limited number of core concepts and assigned gestures. This paper aims to create a sign language system that will enhance communication within the deaf community. The focus is to implement a software model for sign language recognition using a classifier. The approach involves recognizing and analyzing gestures using principal component analysis features and Hu-Moment features. Several classifiers are utilized to measure accuracy and performance.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of Quantum Feature Representation for Leveraging Fused Descriptor Definition in Breast Cancer Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Breast cancer remains a global health challenge, driving the need for advanced diagnostic tools that ensure timely detection and better patient outcomes. This research introduces an innovative diagnostic method that enhances manually engineered features and deep learning-based features with quantum machine learning (QML) based feature representation techniques to improve the accuracy of breast cancer classification. Our results demonstrate that the Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC) consistently outperforms other methods, particularly when paired with Uniform Local Binary Pattern (uLBP) features, achieving an accuracy of 94.3%. Additionally, the fusion of Color Histogram (CH) features with QSVC assisted representation learning features achieves precision and recall rates of 96.6% and 96.3% respectively, highlighting superiority of quantum-based descriptor definition. In comparison, deep features from Inception-ResNet-V2 merely reach an accuracy of 87%, indicating limited effectiveness due to the limitations in non-linear quantum classification tasks. However, the integration of quantum representation learning across all feature sets significantly improves classification performance, particularly when fused with handcrafted or deep features. This study underscores the effectiveness of QML in capturing richer and more discriminative breast cancer characteristics. These findings pave the way for more precise, quantum-enhanced diagnostic tools in the pursuit against breast cancer, offering new avenues for clinical application and market growth.

articleTitle: Handwriting Anomalies and Learning Disabilities through Recurrent Neural Networks and Geometric Pattern Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Dyslexia and dysgraphia are learning disabilities that profoundly impact reading, writing, and language processing capabilities. Dyslexia primarily affects reading, manifesting as difficulties in word recognition and phonological processing, where individuals struggle to connect sounds with their corre-sponding letters. Dysgraphia, on the other hand, affects writing skills, resulting in difficulties with letter formation, spacing, and alignment. The coexistence of dyslexia and dysgraphia complicates diagnosis, requiring a nuanced approach capable of adapting to these complexities while accurately identifying and differentiating between the disorders. This study utilizes advanced geometrical patterns and recurrent neural networks (RNN) to identify handwriting anomalies indicative of dyslexia and dysgraphia. Handwriting is first standardized, followed by feature extraction that focuses on baseline deviations, letter connectivity, stroke thickness, and other anomalies. These features are then fed into an RNN-based autoencoder to identify irregularities. Initial results demonstrate the ability of this RNN model to achieve state-of-art performance on combined dyslexia and dysgraphia detection, while showing the challenges associated with complex pattern adaptation of deep-learning to a diverse corpus of about 33,000 writing samples.

articleTitle: Detection of SQL Injection Attacks Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: As listed in the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), injections are one of the most frequent threats to web applications. SQL injections (SQLi) took precedence among the injections. This research focused on SQLi attack detection with the aid of Machine Learning (ML) techniques. Standing strong on the thorough literary review, the study tried to find a meaningfully capable set of ML algorithms that could be utilized to design and develop a real-time SQLi attack detection model. The research experiment utilized K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF) to fulfill the primary research aim, which is the detection of SQLi attacks. The research used a dataset which consisted of 53,261 data points of both SQLi attack payloads and non-malicious payloads. The SQLi attack payloads covered a wide range of different SQL statements. After the implementation of the experimental designs for three separate ML models, the performance results metrics were generated. As the ML model performance results metrics, it uses classification accuracy, classification error, precision, true positive rate, false positive rate, and specificity. The KNN algorithm achieved 99.55% accuracy, while RF achieved 87.72% and the SVM achieved 98.28%. The KNN algorithm secured the highest rate of accuracy among the three models for SQLi attack detection. The findings of the research show the potential of ML models in SQLi attack detection. The research results can be utilized for the development of ML-enabled attack detection solutions particularly for web applications.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Optimization for Urban and Vertical Agriculture Planning: A Multi-Model Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Urban agriculture has emerged as a critical strategy for enhancing food security, mitigating urban heat islands, and promoting community well-being in densely populated areas. However, the complexity of urban environments poses significant challenges for effective planning and implementation. This paper presents an AI-driven framework to optimize urban and vertical agriculture planning by leveraging advanced machine learning models, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Spiking Neural Networks (SNN), and Large Language Models (LLM). The proposed framework integrates diverse dataset that includes as socioeconomic data, geographic information, and urban zoning regulations to provide actionable insights for decision-makers. The Spiking Neural Network model demon-strated superior predictive accuracy in identifying optimal sites for urban agriculture by effectively handling complex patterns and temporal dynamics in the data. Additionally, the integration of an LLM-powered chatbot into a user-friendly web application enhances interactivity and supports real-time decision-making, guiding users through the prediction process with context-specific recommendations. Experimental results validate the robustness and scalability of the framework across various urban settings, demonstrating its potential to transform urban agriculture practices by providing precise, data-driven recommendations. The findings of this study highlight the transformative potential of AI in urban planning and agriculture, offering a novel approach to fostering sustainable urban development and food security. Future research will focus on expanding the dataset, refining model performance, and enhancing the application's capabilities to support more complex user queries.

articleTitle: Leveraging Fuzzy Logic for Accurate Compound Noun Extraction in Textual Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The extraction of compound nouns from textual documents poses a significant challenge due to the complex and variable nature of linguistic structures. Traditional approaches struggle to accurately capture the nuanced semantics of compound nouns because they rely strictly on exact matches. In this research, we emphasize the importance of using fuzzy logic to address the challenges stemming from ambiguity and imprecision in extracting compound nouns. By leveraging the flexibility of fuzzy logic, we propose a novel approach that exceeds the limitations of traditional methods. Our method embraces the adaptability of fuzzy logic and offers a powerful and context-aware solution for extracting compound nouns. Through empirical evaluation and comparison with traditional approaches, our fuzzy logic-based methodology demonstrates superior performance in capturing the diverse expressions of compound nouns. By incorporating fuzzy logic, our approach excels in handling the variations and uncertainties present in natural language, ultimately providing a more accurate and nuanced representation of compound nouns in textual documents. This research not only advances the field of compound noun extraction but also highlights the effectiveness of fuzzy logic in overcoming challenges associated with the intricacies of language in information extraction tasks.

articleTitle: Classifying Programming Ability: A Machine Learning Approach Using Debugging Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The high failure rate in introductory programming courses (CS1) remains a persistent challenge, prompting research into predictive models that can identify struggling students early. This study investigates the potential of using debugging performance metrics as predictors of programming ability in novice programmers. We examine the statistical association between debugging performance -measured by correctness levels and debugging time- and overall programming ability, as well as the effectiveness of machine learning models in classifying students as high or low achievers based on these metrics. Using data collected from students enrolled in a CSI course, we employ Student's t-test to analyze this association and find that correctness levels are significantly higher among high achievers. We then train and evaluate three machine learning models-Random Forest, k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), and Binary Logistic Regression-using 1,000 iterations of out-of-sample bootstrap validation. Our results demonstrate that all models show promising predictive performance, with Random Forest achieving the highest accuracy (0.86), recall (0.81), precision (0.92), and F1 score (0.85).

articleTitle: Advances and Challenges in Automated Agriculture: Integrating 5G Wireless Technology with IoT, Cloud Computing and Robotics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The agricultural sector is undergoing a transition as automation and robotics converge and evolve. The current labor shortage and the growing need to increase yields are driving innovations in automated agriculture. Automated systems are gradually replacing traditional farming that relies on manpower. The Internet of Things (IoT) with 5G technology has become the key to these traditional automated irrigation systems. The system collects data from soil moisture, rainfall and temperature sensors thus uploads it to the cloud to store data and analyze it to make intelligent irrigation decisions. The proposed innovative system uses iterative learning algorithms and training models to identify pests, diseases and flower types. This article discusses in depth the model evolution of automation technology in the agricultural sector, IoT and cloud computing applications in automated agriculture and the growing use of robotics in agricultural operations. Besides that, it also discusses future directions and challenges. In addition, this article explores the potential for cross-platform collaboration and data sharing to advance the progress of this automation model. However, the field still faces challenges due to the decentralized nature of technology development.

articleTitle: Improving Sales Predictions With Autoformer By Integrating ARIMA For Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Accurate sales forecasting is essential for online businesses to optimize inventory and marketing strategies. This paper addresses a significant and timely problem in e-commerce forecasting by proposing a hybrid model combining ARIMA for anomaly detection and Autoformer for long-term prediction. The integration of these models results in improved forecast accuracy, particularly in handling anomalous sales patterns. The Autoformer model, known for its performance in capturing long-term dependencies and seasonal trends, is enhanced by filtering out anomalies in the sales data using ARIMA before training. Our approach leverages historical sales data from an online shop, Technolife, to demonstrate how the detection of anomalous data leads to more accurate predictions. We provide key performance metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and R-squared (R2) and demonstrate that handling anomalies improves forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Hybrid Quantum Neural Network for Rice Leaf Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Indonesia is an agricultural country that was once listed as the third largest country in terms of rice production. Several factors, such as pests and diseases, are factors in Indonesia's decline in rice productivity. This research explores the integration of quantum computing into classical convolutional neural networks (CNN) for the classification of rice leaf diseases. The study utilizes a hybrid quantum neural network (HQNN) model by combining classical CNN with quantum circuits to evaluate the effect of quantum computing in enhancing agricultural disease detection. The dataset comprises 5932 images of rice leaves affected by four distinct diseases, with each image standardized to 300×300 pixels. The HQNN models were benchmarked against traditional CNN, significantly improving classification accuracy. HQNN reached the best training accuracy of 99.93% and validation accuracy of 99.83%. These findings show that quantum computing has great potential in terms of performance, especially when quantum hardware becomes more accessible. The research concludes by suggesting the need for further exploration with more extensive and diverse datasets to realize the benefits of HQNN in diverse agricultural applications fully.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable LNA Using GaN HEMT for C and X-Band Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable low noise amplifier (RLNA) tailored for C and X-band applications encompassing satellite communication and radar systems, utilizing 0.25µm GaN HEMT technology. The RLNA applied a common input stage linked to a common-source stage followed by a PIN diode SPDT switch that operates as cascade and cascode topologies when configured for C and X-bands respectively, both matched to 50-Ohm terminals. Employing transmission lines for biasing and impedance matching in all amplifier stages, the RLNA achieves a high gain above 21 dB in both bands, with noise figures reaching 0.9 dB and 2.2 dB for C and X-bands respectively. The RLNA boasts input/output return losses exceeding -11 dB, upholding signal integrity, while stability is affirmed through assessment. Impressively, the RLNA demonstrates compression points of 28 dBm and 25 dBm for C and X-bands respectively, highlighting its robust design for versatile RF applications.

articleTitle: A Techno-Economic Study on the Prospect of CSP Plant for Different Areas of Dhaka, Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Concentrated solar power (CSP) plant technology is a very important solution to combat the negative impact of the excessive global carbon emission problem. In the present study, optimization of various CSP-related parameters is done for five different locations in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Survey-based measurements also have been done for these areas during 2023–2024. Among these five locations, Rampura seems to be a good option considering stable radiation; Nandipara was better on the basis of low tower height for power generations below 100 MW; and Bashabo was appropiate with it's minimum heliostat count. Nandipara and Bashabo will ensure a low-cost solution on the basis of lower land prices.
